# ISSUE-90 implementation plan

Make `swarm pr work` plan a focused change to the existing implementation. Keep the original approved plan as context, while `PLAN.md` and `TEST_PLAN.md` remain the active revision artifacts reviewed by the existing gate.

## Shape

**Involved.** This crosses fenced coordination state, GitHub evidence retrieval, role bundles, and output projections in both same-repository and fork execution.

## What we know

- `Service.Work` begins/resumes a revision before executing the workflow (`internal/pr/service.go:634`). `BeginPRRevision` clears active artifacts and attestations through `invalidatePRRevisionEvidence` (`internal/lease/manager.go:1688`, `:1737`), losing the approved plan as planner context.
- `ReviewBindings` hashes only active design/test-plan artifacts; `verifyReviewBinding` requires those hashes and authenticated review metadata (`internal/lease/manager.go:1878`, `:1925`). Keeping historical context outside `Artifacts` preserves these semantics.
- `compileExecutionBundle` already separates PR bundles from issue bundles (`internal/workflow/engine.go:985`); `CompilePRHarnessBundleAt` currently only adds a PR pointer (`internal/workspace/pr.go:22`).
- CI is already refreshed before planning (`internal/workflow/engine.go:572`) and again at the developer boundary (`internal/workflow/ci_evidence.go:7`). `RenderCIEvidence` bounds the complete report at 256 KiB and quotes all remote values (`internal/workspace/ci_evidence.go:16`, `:55`). Reuse this path.
- GitHub review retrieval deliberately returns metadata without bodies or inline comments (`internal/tracker/github.go:884`); its review type has no body (`internal/tracker/tracker.go:92`). A separate evidence API is needed.
- Runtime role instructions load `.swarm/prompts/<role>.md` from the approved base (`internal/harness/scaffold.go:734`). Shipped templates are embedded separately (`internal/harness/scaffold.go:28`). Updating templates cannot by itself activate revision guidance in existing approved repositories.
- Issue status lists active artifacts (`internal/cli/status.go:122`); PR status prints revision/check/review information (`internal/cli/pr.go:160`). PR description review evidence currently renders only active artifacts (`internal/pr/review_projection.go:17`).
- Completion removes `PRRevision` (`internal/lease/manager.go:1819`), so original-plan context stored only on that object would disappear after submission.
- The planner environment is a read-only source snapshot with writable active artifacts; `git status --short` reports no Git repository. No implementation tests have been run during planning.

## What we're assuming

- “Change only internal/harness/templates prompts” restricts **prompt-file changes**, not all source changes: bundle/state/output acceptance criteria require Go changes. Verify this interpretation during plan review; no protected `.swarm/` source files will be edited.
- A complete, current design/test-plan pair with `VerifyApproval` success qualifies as previously approved, including under gate `none`. Test missing-pair and stale-binding cases explicitly; gate-none success alone is insufficient.
- Review evidence should include submitted review summaries and inline review comments, with commit/path metadata to distinguish older findings. General PR conversation comments are outside this WorkUnit.

## Open questions

- How should older repositories with unchanged base-pinned prompts receive revision guidance? Step 3 will verify a PR-only trusted context attachment supplements those prompts without loading candidate policy or changing the role-prompt lookup. Shipped prompts will also document the same revision contract.
- How should successive incremental revisions retain necessary context? Step 1 will implement a small plan-context record containing the original approved pair and accepted prior revision pairs. It preserves the original and the applied deltas rather than silently treating the latest delta as a full original plan. Do not build a general history subsystem.
- Live GitHub permissions and fork publication cannot be exercised in this snapshot. HTTP fixtures and the existing fork gateway/coordinator tests cover the implementation; live same-repository/fork smoke checks belong in PR review and do not block implementation.

## Architectural choice

Keep canonical active filenames and artifact types. The first revision snapshots the verified plan pair into coordinator-owned context before invalidation; the new delta is recorded as the ordinary active design/test-plan pair. Original context is informational and never satisfies approval. Persist context on issue state so it survives completion and is returned through the existing fork gateway.

Alternatives considered: retaining the original in active `Artifacts` risks treating it as the revision and reusing approval; new revision artifact types would require changing gate and digest handling; reconstructing originals from PR text or local files would accept untrusted authority. Separate coordinator-owned context avoids these problems.

## Exact touchpoints

- `internal/lease/manager.go`: `IssueState`, `BeginPRRevision`, completion and invalidation interactions; add `internal/lease/revision_plan.go` for plan-context types, verified snapshot selection, and copying helpers. Add `revision_plan_test.go` and extend existing lifecycle/approval tests.
- `internal/tracker/tracker.go`: separate optional review-evidence interface and typed summary/comment records. Add `internal/tracker/review_evidence.go`; implement bounded GitHub retrieval in `github.go` (or a focused `github_review_evidence.go`) and an empty local implementation in `local.go`. Keep metadata status API behavior unchanged. Add HTTP fixture tests.
- `internal/pr/service.go`: `Service.Work`, evidence retrieval and forwarding. Add `internal/pr/revision_plan_test.go`; extend `service_test.go` fork gateway fixtures.
- `internal/workflow/engine.go`: `WorkOptions`, `compileExecutionBundle`, role task prompts and interactive bundle path; add a focused revision context helper in `internal/workflow/revision_plan.go` if needed. Extend `engine_test.go` and existing CI/reviewer policy tests.
- `internal/workspace/pr.go`: `CompilePRHarnessBundleAt` accepts explicit revision context. Add `internal/workspace/revision_plan.go` and tests for safe materialization, evidence quoting, and bundle contents. Reuse `ci_evidence.go` normalization/quoting principles without changing CI budgets.
- `internal/harness/templates/swarm/prompts/{planner,reviewer,developer}.md` only for prompt-file edits; `internal/harness/scaffold_test.go` for shipped-template checks.
- `internal/cli/status.go`, `internal/cli/pr.go`: distinguish original and revision plans in text/JSON. Add a shared CLI plan-summary helper if needed and targeted status tests.
- `internal/pr/review_projection.go` and tests: include original and revision plan sections in the existing managed description attachment.
- `docs/developer.md`: update “Continuing an Existing PR” only.

## Implementation sequence

1. **Preserve verified plan context within the existing fenced transition.** Add optional, backward-compatible issue-state context with original design/test pair, their digests, task/base/policy identity, and accepted preceding revision pairs when needed. On a new work revision, select/copy complete verified artifacts inside `BeginPRRevision` before clearing active evidence. Never accept a context body, approval, or identity from a fork request or worktree. Resumes retain the same context and pending revision; rejected plans are never promoted. Preserve context after submission; each later work cycle incorporates the previously accepted delta once. Missing/unapproved pairs use the first-plan path. Treat incompatible task/policy identity as ineligible context, rather than inventing approval. Keep existing rebase and issue-work behavior unchanged; context is consumed only by work revisions. Test old serialized states without the new field.
2. **Fetch review evidence through the coordinator.** Introduce a separate optional reader for `pulls/<N>/reviews` summary bodies and `pulls/<N>/comments` inline bodies, including IDs, URLs, author, state, commit SHA, path/line when available. Use context cancellation, explicit request/page/record and response byte bounds (reuse bounded HTTP patterns from `github_comment_bounds_test.go`). Proposed ceilings: 10 pages per endpoint, 100 records/page, 1 MiB response/page, 8 KiB per text body, 128 KiB complete rendered review report. Stop fetching when the evidence budget is exhausted and mark truncation; propagate transport/auth failures with actionable errors rather than pretending no comments exist. Local/unsupported readers yield explicit no-evidence context. Fetch only during actual `Work`, using the linked upstream PR in fork mode; status/dry-run must not download bodies.
3. **Compile explicit revision bundles.** Pass persisted plan context and fetched evidence through the PR workflow, including interactive planner pauses and reviewer staging/resume paths. Materialize `ORIGINAL_PLAN.md`, `ORIGINAL_TEST_PLAN.md`, and, when applicable, preceding accepted deltas in a clearly labeled context attachment. Write `PR_REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md` using root-bound `safefs`, UTF-8/control normalization, per-line block quotation and delimiter-safe fencing; quote metadata too. Enforce the rendered-byte cap, indicate omissions, and remove stale attachments when revision context is absent. Reference current bounded `CI.md` when present, after existing refresh. Include the actual original pair in the role-accessible bundle and point planner/reviewer/developer to it; never label it as a superseded failed attempt. Add trusted PR-only revision-mode guidance to compiled context/task prompts so approved older role prompts still work. Do not replace base-pinned policy with embedded or candidate prompts. Reviewer snapshot receives the same context files. Keep diagnostic bodies outside authoritative artifact and approval fields.
4. **Define and apply the delta contract.** Shipped planner instructions and compiled revision guidance require `PLAN.md` to list each proposed change, its finding/comment/check reference or operator-request reason, affected WorkUnit acceptance criterion, exact implementation touchpoints, and verification. Do not restate unchanged original content. `TEST_PLAN.md` describes changed tests and checks, referring to original coverage for unchanged criteria. Reviewer compares the delta with original/accepted context and WorkUnit, checks scope and evidence, and emits the existing verdict format. Developer starts from the existing PR implementation, follows only the active revision changes, and runs required checks. First plans retain the existing full-plan behavior. Continue using the existing configured agent/human/none gate and `ReviewBindings` on active revision artifacts. No approval algorithm or gate relaxation.
5. **Project both plans.** Add explicitly labeled original approved plan/test-plan and active revision plan/test-plan summaries/digests to issue/PR text status; JSON exposes their bodies and identities from state. In the managed PR review-evidence attachment, show the original pair, preceding accepted deltas if present, and current revision pair with distinct headings. Preserve human description/title and existing marker replacement behavior. After completion, the latest revision remains distinguishable from the original even though `PRRevision` is cleared. Legacy states without context keep current output.
6. **Document and validate.** Explain focused revision plans, evidence inputs, unchanged configured review gate, interactive filenames/staging, and original/revision visibility in the existing developer guide. Retain actual CLI syntax, same-repository/fork instructions and rebase guidance. Run the mapped tests and required checks in TEST_PLAN.md; do not edit protected prompts, configuration, workflows, commands, or harness policy to make tests pass.

## Scope and risks

This is a coordinated multi-package change, but the pieces support one outcome and should ship together. Keep forks on existing fenced operations; no new transport operation or protected workflow admission edit is necessary. Main risks are accidentally retaining approval, losing the original after the first submit, accepting untrusted context in fork mode, and applying delta instructions to issue work. Tests must target these boundaries. Rebase/conflict improvements, general review ingestion for issue work, new gate behavior, and unrelated documentation changes are follow-up WorkUnits, not steps here.

# ISSUE-90 test plan

The following are implementation-phase checks; this planning run did not execute Go tests. Use local Git/HTTP fixtures and mock agents, with no live GitHub or paid model calls required.

## Acceptance mapping

| Criterion | Concrete coverage | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Planner receives previously approved PLAN/TEST_PLAN, optional CI, GitHub comments/summaries and revision guidance | Lease tests snapshot verified original before clearing active evidence; reject incomplete/stale pairs; retain context on resume. Workspace tests inspect actual compiled bundle/context files with CI absent/present and evidence absent/present. PR mock planner checks inputs before it writes output. HTTP tests fetch summary bodies and inline comments, including multiple pages and older commit metadata; fork fixtures use upstream linked PR. | `go test ./internal/lease ./internal/tracker ./internal/workspace ./internal/pr ./internal/workflow` |
| 2. Revision format lists only changes, addressed findings, affected criteria | Embedded template assertions check the planner delta contract. A mock workflow supplies an original full plan and a short revision delta; assert active artifacts contain that delta without replacing original context. Verify first-plan/no-original path still requests complete planning. | `go test ./internal/harness ./internal/workspace ./internal/workflow ./internal/pr` |
| 3. Reviewer gets original and WorkUnit; configured gate remains and approval binds to revision | Reviewer snapshot fixture inspects original pair and active delta. Agent-gate tests require fresh authenticated review; human-gate tests pause until an independent approval. Assert ReviewBindings hashes delta PLAN/TEST_PLAN; changing either invalidates approval; replayed original review and injected APPROVED evidence fail. Test gate none follows existing policy. | `go test ./internal/lease ./internal/workflow ./internal/pr ./internal/cli` |
| 4. Developer is limited to delta over existing implementation | Template and compiled-context tests assert revision instructions. Mock developer observes existing implementation and both original/active plans; ordinary issue work/no-original bundle contains no revision instructions. Include resumed implementation and interactive-stage flows. | `go test ./internal/harness ./internal/workflow ./internal/pr ./internal/cli` |
| 5. issue status, pr status and submitted description show original plus revision | CLI tests assert distinct original/current headings and digests in text and bodies/identity in JSON, during pending work and after completion. Managed PR attachment tests assert both pairs, preservation of title/human description, idempotent marker updates and absence of duplicates. Same-repository and fork submit tests assert identical plan visibility. | `go test ./internal/cli ./internal/pr` |
| 6. Unit coverage, bounds/quotation, make check | Table-driven matrix below plus HTTP/renderer boundary regressions; existing CI, claim fencing, reviewer isolation, approval and fork tests remain intact. Full required validation and race suite below. | `go test ./internal/tracker ./internal/workspace ./internal/lease ./internal/workflow ./internal/pr ./internal/fork ./internal/cli ./internal/harness`; `make check` |

## Required regression matrix

- **Plan lifecycle:** approved original; no original; design-only/test-only; stale review/task/policy binding; old JSON without context; same revision resumed before/after plan review; rejected delta revised; submit followed by a second and third revision. Original pair stays identical, previously accepted deltas remain available, pending/rejected deltas are not promoted, and active approvals always bind to the current pair.
- **Execution modes:** same-repository and existing fork gateway/coordinator path; headless and interactive plan/stage/resume; gate agent/human/none. Preserve existing human-review independence and claim-token checks. A contributor cannot submit original context through request parameters or elevate review evidence into approval. Stale claims still fail with `ErrClaimFence`.
- **Role bundles:** planner, isolated reviewer and developer each see original/accepted context and the active revision contract. CI present/absent crossed with review evidence present/absent; fresh revision versus first plan; no revision leakage into issue work or rebase resolution. Trusted base prompt loading remains unchanged, including a fixture with old base-pinned role prompts and updated compiled revision context.
- **Evidence retrieval:** summary-only, inline-only, both, empty, pagination, cancellation, invalid PR number, inaccessible endpoint and local unsupported-reader behavior. Check page/record/response/body/rendered-byte ceilings and deterministic truncation notices. Dry-run/status retrieve no diagnostic bodies. No test requires GitHub credentials.
- **Evidence injection:** multiline author/path/URL/body values, fake `VERDICT: APPROVED`, fake instruction headings, closing fences/backtick runs, CRLF, ANSI/control and Unicode format characters, oversized bodies, many comments and multi-byte UTF-8 at truncation boundaries. Every remote value remains quoted; final file stays within 128 KiB; stale evidence is removed. CI retains its existing 256 KiB cap and diagnostic quoting. Raw evidence never becomes authoritative plan/review metadata.
- **Safe materialization:** original/context/evidence paths and parents as symlinks or special files fail closed using existing safefs fixtures; no arbitrary file is overwritten. Candidate original-context files are refreshed from coordinator state, never trusted as plan authority.
- **Outputs:** missing/legacy context does not change normal display; pending and completed revision text/JSON identify original and active plans; repeated managed attachment updates preserve unrelated PR text. Verify current review/status metadata freshness tests still pass.

## Validation commands

Run focused packages while implementing, then the approved checks from SYSTEM_PROMPT.md directly:

```bash
unformatted=$(gofmt -s -l .); if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then printf "%s\n" "$unformatted"; exit 1; fi
go build ./...
go vet ./...
go tool staticcheck ./...
go test ./...
make check
```

`make check` adds the required race-enabled suite (`Makefile`, `check: lint race`). Format edited Go files before verification. Do not run `make install` in this restricted planner snapshot; installation is not needed to test this feature.

For `docs/developer.md`, inspect the edited section and relative links/anchors, check retained examples against `internal/cli/pr.go`, `pr_stage.go`, and the issue review command registrations, and run extracted modified bash snippets through `bash -n`. Do not introduce new flags.

## Review-only environment checks

If maintainers have GitHub access, smoke-test one linked same-repository PR and one contributor fork PR: start work, inspect original and delta context, satisfy the configured gate, validate, explicitly submit, and inspect the managed description plus both status commands. Confirm summary/inline comments are visible as evidence. These checks are supplementary and do not block sandbox implementation; HTTP fixtures and coordinator tests provide automated coverage.

VERDICT: APPROVED

## Non-blocking notes for the developer

1. **Second invalidation path.** `BeginPRRevision` clears evidence in two places. One is the fresh `work` revision. The other is when a pending `rebase` revision is converted to `work` (`internal/lease/manager.go` around the `st.PRRevision.Intent == "rebase"` branch). Snapshot the verified pair before **both** calls to `invalidatePRRevisionEvidence`. Add a lifecycle test for rebase → work conversion.
2. **"Approved" under gate `none`.** `VerifyApproval` returns success under `none` after checking only the task digest, and `BeginPRRevision` has no `*WorkUnit`. The selection helper should therefore compare the state-held `TaskDigest`/`PolicyTreeDigest` and require a complete design + test-plan pair, as the assumption says. It must not call `VerifyApproval` on its own.
3. **Compiled revision guidance.** Keep the trusted guidance added in Go short and supplementary to the base-pinned role prompts. It should not grow into a second copy of the template prompts.
4. **History record.** Limit the "accepted preceding revision pairs" list in size, or render only the needed deltas, so repeated revisions cannot grow issue state or bundles without bound.
5. **PII invariant.** The PR description attachment and status output must not include local worktree paths, hostnames or env values. Render plan bodies and digests only.

## Follow-up suggestions (not part of this WorkUnit)

- Ingest general PR conversation comments (not review comments) as evidence.
- Keep original-plan context across a rebase whose published head changed outside SwarmOS.

## Developer report

# ISSUE-90 implementation

PR work now preserves the original approved plan/test pair in coordinator-owned issue state before clearing active artifacts. Each revision uses the ordinary active design/test-plan artifacts, so existing gates and approval digests continue to apply to the revision. Accepted preceding deltas survive submission and are deduplicated; history is limited to 16 accepted deltas, with an actionable error instead of silently discarding context. Missing or ineligible original pairs retain full planning.

GitHub review summaries and inline comments are retrieved only for actual PR work, including the upstream PR identity in fork mode. Retrieval bounds pages, records, response bytes, text fields, and total evidence. Reports normalize controls and UTF-8, quote every remote value inside delimiter-safe fences, mark truncation, and remain within 128 KiB. Existing CI evidence limits are unchanged.

PR planner, reviewer, and developer bundles receive safely materialized original plans, accepted deltas, and concise trusted revision guidance while retaining base-pinned role prompts. Shipped role templates define focused revision planning and implementation. Issue/PR status and managed PR descriptions distinguish original and current plans, including after submission. The continuing-PR developer guide explains the workflow.

Regression coverage includes eligible/ineligible originals, authenticated approval replay, changed plan/test digests, rejected deltas, legacy JSON, successive deltas, rebase-to-work conversion, resumes, history limits, role bundles, CI/review evidence combinations, hostile evidence, HTTP limits and failures, symlink rejection, same-repository/fork visibility, and status/dry-run evidence isolation.

Validation passed on the final source:

- Repository-wide gofmt check.
- `go build ./...`.
- `go test ./...`.
- `make check` (`go vet ./...`, `go tool staticcheck ./...`, and `go test -race ./...`).
- Bash parsing of continuing-PR documentation examples; retained CLI syntax checked against existing command registrations.

Live GitHub publication smoke checks remain supplementary maintainer checks as specified in TEST_PLAN.md. No publication or coordinator staging was performed by this agent subprocess.
